UKMTO received a report of an incident 70NM southwest of Aden, Yemen. A vessel was approached and hailed by one white skiff, with five persons onboard. This was followed by an exchange of small arms fire. Two additional skiffs were also reported the in the vicinity. Update 001 UKMTO have been made aware that only warning shots were fired and no weapons were directed at either vessel. This incident has now been downgraded to suspicious activity. Authorities are continuing to investigate.

The skiff hailed the tug on VHF and ordered the tug to stop. The tug did not comply, and warning shots were fired by the skiff. The tug responded with warning shots from their embarked security team and departed the area. Yemeni representatives noted that the skiff was being operated by a local joint security force and warning shots were fired by the skiff to establish communication with the vessel for identification and verification means. JMIC encourages vessels transiting the area to implement Best Management Practices- Maritime Security, and report any suspicious activity (with the details of the suspicious boat and personnel onboard) to UKTMO at the earliest convenience. heading: ADVISORY
description: Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity, kinetic activity, or electronic interference to UKMTO.

JMIC Guidance to Mariners: • Vessels are advised to transit with caution and conduct enhanced risk assessments. • Maintain a listening watch on VHF Channel 16 and be prepared to respond to hails. • Be alert to the risk of misidentification and the potential effects of electronic interference. • Where practicable, vessels may consider increasing distance from military units to reduce risk. • Report suspicious activity, kinetic activity, electronic interference, or abnormal VHF communications to UKMTO or MSCIO The situation remains extremely dynamic, UKMTO will continue to monitor and issue further updates as information becomes available. Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity, kinetic activity, or electronic interference to UKMTO.

JMIC is aware of open-source media reporting and vessel-to-vessel VHF communications indicating that transit through the Strait of Hormuz has been ‘banned’ by Iranian authorities. At the time of this advisory, no official closure of the Strait of Hormuz has been formally communicated to the maritime industry through recognized maritime safety channels. Specifically: - No NAVAREA navigational warning has been issued declaring closure. - No IMO-recognized Maritime Safety Information (MSI) broadcast has suspended transit passage. - No hydrographic notice to mariners has declared an exclusion zone with coordinates applicable to international shipping. While vessels have reported receiving VHF hails from Iranian Revolutionary Guard elements indicating transit restrictions, such communications do not constitute a legally recognized suspension of transit passage under international maritime law. Commercial traffic, though reduced in volume, continues to transit the Strait. LEGAL CONTEXT The Strait of Hormuz qualifies as a strait used for international navigation under the transit passage regime of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).
